args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After deploying checkout-api v2.3.1 to production (us-east, us-west, eu-west), the service failed health checks with an 18% error rate. (v2.3.1-rc had also been unhealthy in staging.) checkout-api was rolled back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is 0.2%. Next step: find the root cause in v2.3.1 before deploying it again.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions and opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged on-call.

- **Cause:** Release v2.3.1 is running in us-east, us-west and eu-west. Since it went out, the service has been failing health checks with an 18% error rate.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. us-east, us-west and eu-west now all run it. A status check afterwards shows the service is healthy, with the error rate down to 0.2%. Since v2.3.0 had been healthy in production before, the change-manager approval rule didn't apply.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 covers the failure, the rollback and the recovery, and notes that v2.3.1 needs a root-cause review before it's deployed again.

The deployment history shows the release candidate for v2.3.1 (v2.3.1-rc) was already unhealthy in staging, but v2.3.1 still went to production. It's worth checking why that didn't stop the release.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
